scenario: fingerprint_distance measures each of the 10 traits in units of the population's own std (ddof 0), so the scale is fixed by construction: for the gate's n=15 population the RMS pairwise distance is sqrt(2*D*n/(n-1)) = 4.63. 'seed_mean > 0.05' therefore holds unless the three balanced seeds are almost identical. At fingerprint_k=3, re-measuring the same model with only the measure seed changed gives a mean distance of 2.26 (smallest pair 0.23), about 40-45x the threshold; different training seeds average about 3.0-3.6 and different mixes about 4.3-4.7. In a noise-only null (one model fingerprinted at 20 measure seeds placed in the gate's 12+3 roles), G4 passes 50% of the time and seed_mean never comes near 0.05; with real proxy models the verdict fails about 4% of the time from sampling noise alone, and the gate draws once. Sparse, noisy traits dominate: precision supplies 22% of the balanced seed distance and 43% of the noise distance; for slip_rate and register the measurement noise exceeds the across-seed spread. A full-scale G4 PASS therefore does not show spec §11 criterion 4 ('measurably different' seed fingerprints).
title: G4's 'measurably different' clause (seed distance > 0.05) sits about 40x below the fingerprint's own sampling noise, so it can never fail and G4 passes on pure measurement noise about half the time

scenario: A full gate with seeds 1,2,3 runs only differentiation (G3) and seed variation (G4) for every seed. G5's grown/ungrown arms, G6's code continuations, G7's four preparation runs and G2's legibility starter use self.seeds[0] only, and decide with strict comparisons (grown < ungrown, drop >= 3, recovery >= 50%, ratio <= 0.8) and no seed spread. At quick scale, repeating G5 on seeds 1-6 gave PASS, FAIL, PASS, PASS, PASS, FAIL (differences -0.094 to +0.025 nats). So the real gate can pass or fail G5/G6/G7 by seed alone: a FAIL can start a step-8 iteration chasing noise, or a step-8 change can 'fix' a criterion through noise, or M2 can be built on a lucky PASS. The plan's Task 20 table narrows this to 'seed 1', but no ledger ruling, ADR or spec amendment records dropping the spec's 3-seed requirement (dispatch ruling 4 covers only reusing the seed-1 starter and base).
title: Spec §4.12 says '3 seeds each', but G2, G5, G6 and G7 (and G1) are decided on seed 1 alone with zero-margin thresholds, so verdicts can flip by seed

scenario: The real gate trains g7-web-light and g7-web-thorough (70% web, 4x128, 8.4M tokens) and compares the unknown-word share of 60 web completions. 484 real FineWeb docs through the real apply_noise with the web recipe (30 noise seeds pooled), cut with the real thresholds (light q>=0.15; thorough q>=0.65 plus dedup) and counted the gate's way: light 7.06% vs thorough 5.55% (ratio 0.786) with a 30k general vocab, 9.11% vs 7.46% (0.819) with an in-domain 30k vocab built like build_vocab; per-seed ratio 0.71-0.94. Clean docs alone have 4.9-7.0% unknown words (names, brands, rare words) and supply over half of the unknown words left after thorough cleaning; thorough removes only half of the typo docs by the graded-strength ruling. So even a model that copied its training data perfectly lands on the bar, and a 4x128 model's own non-words push the ratio toward 1. A likely outcome is G7 FAILS although cleaning works, sending the owner into the 'adjust and rerun' loop on GPU time.
title: G7(a) cannot be expected to pass on real data: thorough cleaning lowers the unknown-word share of real web training text only to 79-82% of light's, at or above the 0.8 bar, before the model adds non-words of its own
